title: SessionBlob — shared definition for the result of a proxy login
description:
Cleartext shape of the session material returned by vault/proxy-login/0.1. Like VaultSecret, this is documented for both sides to code-generate against; the wire-form is carried inside an HPKE-sealed envelope.

A SessionBlob represents an active session at the third-party service the VTA logged in to on the holder's behalf. The Companion uses it to operate the session (e.g. inject cookies into the browser, set an Authorization header) without ever seeing the long-term credential. The session has a finite TTL; the Companion MUST discard the blob when `expiresAt` passes.

sessionId.description: Maintainer-assigned opaque id for this session. Used for revoke/refresh operations against the maintainer.

expiresAt.description: Time after which the session material MUST be discarded. The maintainer SHOULD set this conservatively — short TTL is the primary defence against a compromised Companion replaying the session beyond its useful lifetime.

cookies.description: Cookies the Companion injects into the appropriate origin's cookie jar. Order is significant for sites that set multiple cookies with the same name on different paths.

headers.description: HTTP request headers the Companion attaches to outbound requests to the bound origin until `expiresAt`. Typically holds `Authorization: Bearer …`.

localStorage.description: Optional localStorage entries to set on the origin. Used by SPAs that store session material there rather than in cookies.

sessionStorage.description: Optional sessionStorage entries to set on the origin.

bindOrigin.description: The web origin this session is for. Companions MUST refuse to inject the session into any other origin.

refreshHint.description: Tells the Companion when to call back for a refreshed session. `maintainerOnly` = don't refresh on your own. `on401` = call when the third party returns 401. `beforeExpiry` = pre-emptively refresh shortly before `expiresAt`.
